questions.background: The Golden Boot recognizes the World Cup's leading goal scorer, with FIFA's tie-breaking rules determining the winner if players finish level on goals.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : FIFA's official announcement of the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot winner. Resolution Date : Resolve upon confirmation of the award winner at the conclusion of the tournament, whose final is scheduled for July 19, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the player officially awarded the Golden Boot, rather than the Silver Boot or Bronze Boot.
questions.current_reasoning: Significant June 26 Golden Boot shakeup from France 4-1 Norway: Kylian Mbappé started against Norway's second-string XI and went scoreless (hit the bar, 1 assist), finishing the group stage on 4 goals with zero group matches left, while Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé erupted for a 25-minute first-half hat-trick to surge onto 4 goals for #1 contender France. Meanwhile, Erling Haaland was benched vs France (staying on 4 goals) and 2I Norway dropped into a much tougher knockout path (Ivory Coast -> Brazil/Japan -> England/Mexico, ~2.1 expected KO games vs Argentina's tournament-high ~3.4). Lionel Messi (5 goals, 1-goal lead, possible cameo vs Jordan on June 27, softest knockout bracket) separates as clear favorite (29% -> 36%), Mbappé drops (29% -> 22%), Vinícius Júnior trims slightly (9% -> 7.5%), Dembélé enters at 7% (replacing 2-goal Harry Kane at ~6% pending England vs Panama), and Haaland drops (10% -> 6.5%).

local_articles.title: Which teams are in the World Cup round of 32, and what’s the schedule?
local_articles.snippet: have already left their mark. Here’s what you need to know about the round of 32: What is the format of the World Cup knockouts? The top two teams in each of the 12 groups, along with the eight best third-place finishers, advance to the knockouts. The knockout phase begins with the round of 32, introduced at the World Cup following the tournament’s expansion from 32 to 48 teams. Then comes the round of 16, followed by the quarterfinals, semifinals and a playoff for third place. The final is on July 19. The stage-wise breakdown of the tournament’s knockout schedule is: Round of 32: June 28 to July 3 Round of 16: July 4–7 Quarterfinals: July 9–11 Semifinals: July 14–15 Bronze medal match: July 18 Final: July 19 Which teams have qualified for the round of 32? So far, 26 teams have punched their ticket to the knockouts. They include: ⚽️ Colombia ⚽️ Argentina ⚽️ France ⚽️ Norway ⚽️ Germany ⚽

questions.title: Which country will win the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup?
questions.background: The Women's T20 World Cup is the International Cricket Council's world championship for women's national teams in Twenty20 cricket.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official tournament final result published by the International Cricket Council, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Resolve when the winner of the 2026 tournament is established by the final's official result. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the winning country.
questions.current_reasoning: Major June 24-25 Women's T20 World Cup results sharpen the semifinal and title picture: (1) Hosts England (4-0, +2.342 NRR) became the first team to clinch the semifinals by comfortably beating West Indies by 38 runs at Lord's (186/7 vs 148/5) even without injured captain Nat Sciver-Brunt, who is progressing well for a semifinal return (+3% to 29%); (2) Australia remain dominant at 4-0 (+4.724 NRR, tournament-best 5.95 powerplay economy), nudging up to 51%; (3) South Africa crushed Netherlands by 88 runs (208/1, Tazmin Brits 114*) to reach 3-1 with only Bangladesh left on June 28 (~62% to claim Group A's second spot, holding at 8%); (4) India beat Bangladesh by 5 wickets (3-1) despite dropping four catches, but now likely must upset unbeaten Australia on June 28 (or rely on Bangladesh beating SA) to reach the semis, dropping India from 8% to 5.5%; (5) West Indies (3-1, +0.008 NRR) were exposed by England and now project as Group B runners-up facing Australia in the semis, trimming them from 8% to 6%.

questions.current_reasoning: Critical June 24-25 update: England captain Nat Sciver-Brunt is sidelined with a calf injury—she missed England's 38-run win over West Indies and has been officially ruled out of their final group game vs New Zealand on June 27, dropping her from 9% out of the top five (~2-3% max if returning for semis). In her absence, Danni Wyatt-Hodge surged to the top of England's POTT candidates with a Player of the Match 65 off 42 balls at Lord's (entering at 10%), while stand-in captain Charlie Dean (7 wickets in 4 matches, 2/31 vs West Indies) enters at 7% alongside Sophie Ecclestone (6.5%) for a 29%-title-favorite England side. For 51% title favorites Australia, BBC noted Australia's wickets are evenly spread across seven bowlers with none in the tournament's top five wicket-takers, further boosting two-time POTM all-rounder Ellyse Perry (42.33 avg / 138 SR, 4 wkts at 5.75 econ) from 18% to 21%, with Georgia Wareham steady at 9%.

questions.title: Which team will win the England–India T20 international series in July 2026?
questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Two concrete updates shift the five-match England-India T20I series (July 1-11 in England) from 56-44 India to a razor-thin 51-49 home edge for England: (1) India suffered a shock 34-run defeat to an injury-depleted Ireland (missing Stirling, Adair, Josh Little, and Campher) in the 1st T20I in Belfast on June 26—India's first loss to Ireland in any format—as their reshuffled middle order (new captain Shreyas Iyer 3 off 7, Sanju Samson 0, Ishan Kishan, Sundar) collapsed for 148 against hard-length UK pace and their Bumrah/Hardik-less bowling leaked 152 runs in the final 14 overs after having Ireland 30/3; (2) ECB's confirmed 17-man squad features near-full-strength home firepower under Harry Brook including fit Jofra Archer, Jos Buttler, Phil Salt, Will Jacks, Jacob Bethell, Sam Curran, Adil Rashid, Saqib Mahmood, and Josh Tongue. Combining England's home pace advantage and near-full-strength roster against a Bumrah-, Hardik-, and Suryakumar-less India (even accounting for T20 high variance and India's strong batting depth) warrants a 7% calibration shift to England 51% / India 49%.

local_articles.snippet: Shreyas Iyer had to wait for his time, but it has indeed come sooner rather than later. The right-handed batter replaced Suryakumar Yadav as the T20I captain earlier this year; however, his first match in charge didn't go according to plan as the Men in Blue went down by 34 runs against Ireland in the first T20I of the two-match series in Belfast on Friday. Iyer, who wasn't a part of the T20 World Cup 2026-winning squad, played his first T20I for India on Friday after a gap of two years. Former England captain Michael Vaughan recently weighed in on the appointment of Shreyas as the skipper, saying he thought Ricky Ponting would become India coach when he first heard about Iyer's elevation in the T20I setup.
